display.title: Matzliach and the Mitzvah of Negel Vasser, Part 3
display.summary_short: The passengers gladly take Matzliach's gold. Alone and penniless in a forest, he hides from armed robbers and slips into their hidden cave full of treasure.
display.summary_long: The passengers agree to share Matzliach's gold in return for a little less water, and every day he receives a second container, so he can wash, say brachos, put on tefillin and daven. When the caravan leaves the desert, Matzliach, now without money or a camel, thanks the chief, who had also let him rest on Shabbos, and sets off alone through a forest with his tallis and tefillin, eating berries and trusting in Hashem. At nightfall he finds a stone oven with warm coals, and before lying down he searches for water and finds a clear pond to fill his negel vasser cup. Suddenly a band of armed robbers arrives, dragging a prisoner in chains: the caravan chief. Hiding in a tree, Matzliach watches them roll aside a great rock and enter a hidden cave. In the morning, after they leave, he levers the rock open with a branch, eats only food he knows is kosher, and discovers an underground hall filled with treasures. To be continued.
display.lesson: Hashem watches over a Jew who trusts in Him and keeps His mitzvos even when alone.
